impact_scope.description: S1 introduces the public SHA-256 hasher checksum callable anchored by the selected declaration; it and its containing module are absent in S0.

evidence: S0 has no matching declaration in the selected source file.
The anchored public hasher.checksum_bitvec256 callable and SHA-256 module do not exist in S0, so H0 has no S0 exposure obligation for this unit.
S1 declares pub func hasher.checksum_bitvec256() base.bitvec256 in std/sha256/common_sha256.wuffs.
H0 enables only AUX__BASE, AUX__JSON, BASE, and JSON modules; it neither enables SHA-256 nor constructs or calls a SHA-256 hasher.
H0 exclusively exercises JSON decoding paths, so no existing one-hop caller reaches the new checksum callable.

new_harness_obligation.description: To expose the new anchored callable, H0 must enable the SHA-256 module and add a SHA-256 hasher lifecycle that supplies input through update and calls checksum_bitvec256; none of those H0 actions was necessary in S0.
evidence: The S1 callable is a newly introduced public entry point rather than new internals behind an existing H0-reached caller.
The unchanged harness contains no SHA-256 module configuration or hasher calls.

reason: For the identical anchored unit, Gap(S0,H0) is false because the public callable is absent in S0, while Gap(S1,H0) is true because S1 introduces it and H0 does not compile or invoke its module. This creates concrete new configuration and call obligations, so the truth-table result is NEW and maintenance is needed.
